page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.large is an entry-level, memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 2 burstable vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading, running on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a substantial 480 MB shared L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, while omitting bundled local NVMe storage and dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized for single-threaded bursts rather than sustained multi-threaded parallelism. The instance scores in the top tier for single-core tasks, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2159.0, rapid single-threaded gzip compression at 33.89 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 14.39 GB/sec. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the single physical core configuration, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2719.0 and bottom-decile stress-ng multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also show lower uncached throughput across large blocks, reflecting standard virtualized multi-tenant limits.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i-flex.large provides access to current-generation Intel Xeon silicon and high DDR5 RAM capacity at a reduced operational threshold compared to non-burstable instances. The burstable CPU allocation profile represents an intentional design tradeoff, restricting sustained compute performance in favor of memory allocation density. The instance is well-suited for lightweight in-memory caching tiers, development databases, background workers, and memory-dependent web application serving that experience intermittent traffic patterns.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 burstable vCPUs across 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM at 7 GHz, providing a generous 8:1 memory-to-core ratio without local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs. Performance benchmarks show strong single-threaded capabilities, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2159.0 and fast gzip compression, though multi-core throughput remains restricted due to the single-core topology. The burstable CPU allocation model balances cost efficiency with elevated memory density, establishing the instance as a practical choice for small memory-centric workloads, lightweight database engines, caching layers, and staging environments.
